page.name: Bringing your own provider vs buying credits
page.h1: Bring your own provider accounts vs buying message credits from a platform
page.metaTitle: BYOL vs buying credits — keep your own rates
page.metaDescription: Why the platform connects to accounts you already hold instead of selling credits: your rate stays yours and switching stays a configuration change.
page.lede: We connect to the provider accounts you already pay for, and we never sell you message credits. That one decision sets your rate, your switching cost, and who owns the relationship — everything below follows from it.

sections.h: Why we connect instead of reselling
bullets: Your rate is your rate — nothing is added on top of the price you already negotiated, because there is no balance in the middle to mark up
Your commitment stays with your provider, so a change of tools never strands volume you already bought
You remain the customer of record — for pricing, for registrations, for sender identity
Disconnecting leaves your account untouched: leaving is a configuration change, not a migration

p: A prepaid balance is genuinely simpler to budget — one invoice, one number to watch. What it moves out of view is the rate underneath: you know what you paid, not what the message cost. That is also why leaving a balance-holder means migrating accounts rather than changing a setting.
bullets: Your provider invoice, at your rate — versus one blended balance
Volume commitments you control — versus a balance somebody else holds
Switching tools by changing configuration — versus moving accounts

sections.h: How to get the most out of this model
p: Bring the account you already have and keep the registrations in your own name. The layer adds routing, pacing, receipts and logs on top; everything commercial stays exactly where it was, so there is nothing to unwind if you ever stop.

faq.q: Does Whaleal take a margin on messages?
faq.a: No. There is no credit balance to mark up — you pay your provider directly, and the platform never sits in the middle of the money.

faq.q: Can I start with a single provider?
faq.a: Yes. Connecting one account is a fully supported setup, and it is where most teams start. Routing and failover are there for the day you add a second.

faq.q: What happens to our provider contract if we adopt the platform?
faq.a: It stays yours, on your terms and your rates. The platform is given credentials to send through the account and read status back — nothing more, and nothing that touches the contract.
